  MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Council Chambers, 111 South First Street
  August 10, 2021
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:04 p.m., on Tuesday, August 10, 2021 the Alhambra City Council met in
Council Chambers and via video conference.

PRESENT via video conference:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, PÉREZ
PRESENT:  LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present physically and via video conference: City Manager Binnquist, City Attorney
Montes, Assistant City Manager Garcia, City Clerk Myles, Director of Community Development
Ho

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M21-103

The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956
of the Government Code of the State of California.
CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING

1.  APPLICATIONS FOR VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP TT 74194, RESIDENTIAL
  PLANNED DEVELOPMENT PERMIT RP-17-7, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT CU-17-9
  AND DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE PROPOSED
  VILLAGES AT THE ALHAMBRA PROJECT (PROJECT) WITH 294 NEW, FOR-SALE,
  RESIDENTIAL DWELLING UNITS IN FIVE-STORY STACKED FLAT AND
  TOWNHOME CONFIGURATIONS; 545 NEW RENTAL APARTMENTS IN FIVE-STORY
  STACKED FLAT CONFIGURATIONS; AND UP TO 4,347 TOTAL PARKING SPACES
  TO ACCOMMODATE ALL NEW USES. IT IS EXPECTED THAT IF THE PROJECT IS
  APPROVED THE APPLICANT WILL IMPLEMENT A PARKING REDUCTION
  PURSUANT TO ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 23.52.060. THE PROJECT
  SITE IS LOCATED IN THE PO (PROFESSIONAL OFFICE) ZONE. AN
  ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT REPORT HAS BEEN PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT
  AND WILL ALSO BE CONSIDERED WITH THE PROJECT ALONG WITH A POSSIBLE
  STATEMENT OF OVERRIDING CONSIDERATIONS – F2M17-50, N2M20-163

  At the July 6, 2021 Special City Council meeting, the Council considered the item and
  following a brief discussion the Council continued the item to this evening for the Water
  Quality Control Board to provide a reassessment of the project. Since the Council’s last
  meeting, the Water Quality Control Board submitted a letter and made a presentation at
  the regular meeting of City Council on July 12, 2021 summarizing that previous analysis
  and guidance was still valid and offered additional recommendations. In addition, an
  updated draft of the development agreement has been completed incorporating terms

  1
8-10-21
   negotiated by the two Council Sub-Committees for Council’s consideration. Staff reviewed
  the agreement and provided comments which have been incorporated into the agreement.
  The development agreement included the following provisions: Inclusionary Housing;
  Vapor Mitigation; Hazardous Substances Indemnification (Corner Plan Area – Lot 8);
  Traffic Assessment and Management; Open Space and Community Access; Trees and
  Landscaping; and, Sales Tax Point of Sale Designation. Should the City Council provide
  direction to approve or deny the project, staff would return at the September 13th or other
  special meeting, as determined by the Council, with resolutions reflecting the Council
  direction. In that regard, also attached to the August 10, 2021 report by the Director of
  Community Development were excerpts from the City’s code concerning findings required
  for the entitlements requested for the project. Approval of the project would require the
  Council affirmatively make these required findings based upon information provided over
  the course of the Council’s various public hearings on the matter. Denial would require
  that the Council determine one or more of the required findings could not be made, based
  upon information provided over the course of the public hearings. Should the Council
  direct preparation of approval documents, staff would also work with the Applicant on any
  revisions to the development agreement needed for clarity and implementation.

  Councilmember PÉREZ provided a report of the Subcommittee meetings with the
  Applicant. She stated that they were contacted by the Ratkovich Company representative,
  Brian Saenger, to report that the developer reached out to the California EPA’s Office of
  Environmental Health Hazard Assessment (OEHHA) and the Regional Water Quality
  Control Board to conduct an updated Risk Assessment of the soil samples based on the
  most current testing standards as opposed to the now outdated standards used at the
  time of the first test. The Ratkovich Company requested an extension of about three weeks
  to conduct a full Risk Assessment of the site to resolve many environmental concerns
  raised by Council. Ms. Pérez motioned to continue the meeting to a date specific to allow
  for the Applicant to conduct their Risk Assessment. Councilmember MALONEY seconded
  Ms. Pérez’s motion and added that Council acknowledged the concerns of the public
  regarding potential contamination of the site. He also acknowledged the work conducted
  by the developer previously as well as the fact that the studies conducted at the time did
  not utilize the most current and up to date standards of analysis. He acknowledged the
  Developer’s efforts to conduct a new Risk Assessment as a positive step.

  Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER thanked the Subcommittee for their hard work but
  stated that Council had been more than patient through this process. She stated that the
  applicant had not provided enough information to approve the project at this time.
  However, she stated that there were enough findings to support a denial of the project.
  She listed the number of pending reports and analyses that Council was awaiting. Mayor
  LEE asked that Council consider the current pending motion to continue the meeting.
  Councilmember MAZA supported the motion to continue the meeting in light of new
  information to inform Council’s decision.

  Mayor LEE stated that she believed the proposed full Risk Assessment from the Applicant
  was insignificant due to the previously reported risks of the site. She referred to the report
  from the Regional Water Quality Control Board as further proof that additional testing
  would not address the contamination as is. She stated that she felt she had enough
  information based on the Regional Water Quality Control Board report and did not want to
  wait an additional three weeks. Ms. PÉREZ acknowledged the length of time to consider
  this project and the frustrations it has caused. She reiterated that the updated data was
  important regardless of the future of the current project due to the complications of the

  2
8-10-21
   site itself. She stated that she made it clear to Mr. Saenger that Council would like the
  report to be concluded in a timely manner. She stressed the importance of determining
  the overall safety of neighboring residents. Ms. LEE stated that she believed that the
  developer should clean up the site based on the Regional Water Quality Control Board
  recommendations, regardless of project approval or denial since the developer owned the
  parcel in question. She stated that even if the developer cleaned their site, there were still
  other contaminated parcels which were the responsibility of other property owners. She
  reiterated that there was enough information provide to make a decision regardless of the
  new request for soil sampling. Mr. MALONEY stated that it was likely that regardless of
  Council’s decision on the present project, it was likely that there would be development of
  the site in the future and that it was important for the developer to offer to provide more
  information for the future of the site. He also reasoned that there was a possibility of a
  legal challenge to any potential denial of the project wherein the developer would not have
  to conduct another Risk Assessment.

  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER stated that this site would have to be cleaned up by any owner
  regardless of the current project. She stated that Council needed to review the project
  based on its current merit and not provide additional time to the developer. She stated
  that the project failed on multiple counts such as keeping the community safe from the
  environmental risks and transportation issues. She stated that she was not in favor of
  continuing the project and that they owed it to the community to make a decision. She
  outlined the several points which the developer refused to concede such as inclusionary
  housing, transportation shuttles, and community workforce agreement.

ANDRADE-STADLER:  Councilmember Andrade-Stadler left the meeting at approximately
6:25 p.m.

  Ms. PÉREZ continued to discuss the benefits of receiving a full Risk Assessment from the
  Applicant as a means of determining the type of clean up on the site. She stated that
  without current updated data, the Regional Water Quality Control Board would continue
  to make the same recommendations. She outlined the ways in which new data would drive
  updated recommendations to ensure the best clean-up of the site. Ms. LEE reiterated that
  consideration of the current project was independent of the full Risk Assessment and
  reiterated her previous comments regarding the responsibility of the property owner.

ANDRADE-STADLER:  Councilmember Andrade-Stadler returned to the meeting at
approximately 6:28 p.m.

  Ms. LEE and Ms. PÉREZ continued their discussion.

  Council went on to discuss potential dates to continue the meeting with City Manager
  BINNQUIST and Ms. MOLOUGHNEY. Ms. PÉREZ amended her motion to continue the
  hearing until September 30, 2021 at 6:00 p.m.

  Action Taken:  City Council continued the hearing open to September 30, 2021 at
  6:00 p.m., and deferred taking any additional public testimony until that date, when it was
  anticipated additional information would be available.

  Vote:  Moved:  PÉREZ  Seconded: MALONEY
  Ayes:  MALONEY, PÉREZ, MAZA
  Noes:  LEE, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Absent:  NONE

8-10-21
 ADJOURNMENT: At 6:33 p.m., there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned their meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
